Introduction

Mina Otomonai, known professionally as Chanmina, is a trilingual Korean-Japanese rapper, singer-songwriter and producer. She officially debuted as a soloist on April 18, 2016, independently, before releasing her major label debut album 'Miseinen' in 2017.

Born to a Korean mother and Japanese father, she has a background in ballet, from her mother who was a ballerina. She cites BIGBANG as one of her major musical influences. After she discovered their song "Haru Haru", she quit piano and ballet and began to take Hip-Hop dance lessons.

Due to her unique blend of languages in music, she has collaborated with many artists globally, including Rina Sawayama, Saweetie, Taeyeon, Kang Daniel, Yena and more.

In May 2019 she became the first Japanese artist to appear in the Asian version of Yo! MTV Raps produced by MTV Asia.

Chanmina is also active as an audition producer and judge. Between 2024-2025, she participated as a co-producer with SKY-HI & BMSG for the girl group audition program ‘No No Girls’, to form BMSG's first girl group, HANA. The audition sought out hopefuls who had been rejected or told no by the entertainment industry, society or themselves.

On July 7, 2024, she announced her marriage to South Korean rapper ASH ISLAND. They welcomed their daughter in November.
